Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Linear Systems and Matrices

Matrices at Work

Solving systems and rotating trail maps

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Applications of Matrices
Standards
HSA-REI.C.8, HSA-REI.C.9, HSN-VM.C.12

Students write systems as matrix equations AX = B and solve them with inverses, organise and combine data with matrices, and use matrices to rotate and reflect points on a trail map.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Write a system of linear equations as a matrix equation AX = B.
  • Solve a 2×2 system with X = A−1B.
  • Use matrices to organise and combine real data.
  • Use 2×2 matrices to rotate and reflect points.

3Essential question

How can one matrix equation replace a whole page of elimination?

5MTB connection

Pricing puzzles, team orders and timing splits are systems of equations; writing them as AX = B lets a calculator or spreadsheet solve them instantly.

Trail maps get rotated so “up” matches the direction a rider is facing. That rotation is a matrix multiplication applied to every point on the map, which is how mapping apps do it.

The mathOn the trail
AX = BTicket prices from two group bookings
A−1The “undo” that unlocks the prices
Rotation matrixTurning a trail map to face north-up or heading-up
Reflection matrixMirroring a trail design for the other side of a hill

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Map and Money

Use matrix equations to solve a pricing problem and transformation matrices to reorient a trail map.

You’ll need: Graph paper; Calculator with matrix mode (optional)

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
